data.title: 5E Advanced Materials to Acquire Searles Valley Assets
data.description:
The latest announcement is out from 5E Advanced Materials, Inc. ( (FEAM) ).

On September 14, 2026, 5E Advanced Materials and its subsidiary 5E SVM entered an agreement to acquire Searles Valley Minerals’ key operating assets through a court-supervised Section 363 bankruptcy sale in Delaware. The deal covers production facilities at Argus, Westend and Trona, more than 9,000 acres of Searles Lake brine resources, the Trona Railway short-line railroad, water infrastructure and related utilities, permits and contracts in San Bernardino County, California.

The consideration totals about $3.4 million in cash, 8.3 million shares of 5E common stock and an approximately $6.2 million senior unsecured promissory note, with 5E SVM also assuming specified environmental compliance obligations and other liabilities tied to the assets. Closing, expected in early October 2026, is subject to Bankruptcy Court approval, Surface Transportation Board authorization for the rail assets and the company’s receipt of $10 million in senior secured bridge financing, which will be guaranteed by 5E and secured against 5E SVM’s assets.

Strategically, the acquisition is intended to shift 5E from a pre-revenue developer to an operating critical minerals producer with established commercial output, an existing customer base and near-term revenue, while preserving its Fort Cady boron project as a long-term growth resource. The Searles Valley complex is one of only two operating borate production hubs in the U.S., with integrated cogeneration, rail links and logistics to West Coast ports, and produces refined borates, boric acid, sodium sulfate and salt, broadening 5E’s product platform.

Management argues that combining Searles Valley’s long-life borate resource and infrastructure with Fort Cady’s multi-generational deposit could make 5E the only American-owned borates producer in the U.S. and potentially the second-largest producer in the Western world. The transaction is being executed at what the board describes as a fraction of replacement cost with modest cash outlay, and 5E expects to maintain operations in Trona without interruption and retain a significant portion of Searles Valley’s workforce, underscoring the deal’s implications for domestic critical mineral supply and local employment.
